findings.issue: Candidate signed body does not bind scenario/context identity.
findings.risk: A valid signed evidence object could be spliced across experimental scenarios if epoch/time/sequence values collide or are replayed.
findings.recommendation: Sign an opaque scenario_id/context ID. The ID must not encode topology or fault identity and must remain policy-invisible metadata.

findings.issue: Authorization extraction on signature failure is unresolved.
findings.risk: Forcing authorization to zero on every crypto failure would collapse an independent policy-visible feature into signature validity and alter equal-information semantics.
findings.recommendation: For structurally complete evidence, preserve the parsed signed authorization_value independently of signature_valid. For absent or structurally invalid evidence, set authorization=0 and complete=0.

findings.risk: Including trust or signature success in complete would duplicate other feature meanings.
findings.recommendation: Define complete as structural completeness only: exact canonical length, valid domain separator/version/role/authorization/reserved fields, and parseable mandatory fields. Unknown/untrusted IDs affect their dedicated features, not complete.

findings.risk: Cross-path disagreement and same-path equivocation could be conflated.
findings.recommendation: Define noncontradictory per evidence path. Identical duplicates are not contradictions; two different structurally complete bodies for the same scenario/role/source/epoch/sequence make the path contradictory.

findings.risk: Allowing the producer to sign/select its own freshness bound would let compromised producers weaken freshness enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Keep freshness thresholds in frozen qualifier configuration, not in producer-controlled signed bytes. Sign only issued logical time and epoch.

findings.issue: Registry IDs could accidentally encode topology/fault semantics.
findings.risk: Semantic IDs create avoidable truth/topology leakage and brittle policy coupling.
findings.recommendation: Use opaque nonzero numeric source/key/authority IDs. Topology manifests may alias IDs, but the numeric values must not encode topology or fault class.

findings.issue: Signing-key placement is inconsistent across current design artifacts.
findings.risk: The implementation plan says producer apps emit signed evidence while the current verifier/dependency guardrails prohibit secret keys in flight software.
findings.recommendation: Before producer implementation, explicitly choose either (A) external deterministic test signing service/harness with cFS producers emitting pre-signed evidence, or (B) narrowly scoped producer-only cFS signing components and revise the no-secret-key guardrail to apply to verifier/qualifier/decision FSW. Do not proceed implicitly.

findings.risk: Authority-domain separation cannot be tested faithfully without a stable representation/keying provenance rule.
findings.recommendation: Freeze whether signed authority_id plus harness provenance is sufficient or whether the authority requires a separate cryptographic assertion/key layer.

notes: scenario_id is signed but remains policy-invisible metadata
reserved8 and reserved32 must be zero
explicit byte construction remains mandatory; native struct serialization remains prohibited
64-byte body fits the qualified engineering verifier message capacity exactly

structurally_complete_but_invalid_signat.note: other quality features are independently derived

recommended_qualifier_semantics.completeness: structural only; do not duplicate trust/signature/freshness semantics
recommended_qualifier_semantics.contradiction_scope: same evidence path within signed scenario/epoch/sequence identity
recommended_qualifier_semantics.duplicate_rule: byte-identical duplicate is not a contradiction

blocking_before_freeze: Review/approve candidate v2 scenario binding and 64-byte layout.
Freeze logical-time unit and freshness thresholds.
Freeze source/key/authority registries and test public-key generation provenance.
